chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked:

About a man who divorced his wife with two divorces during the waiting period, then left her until her menstrual periods (quru') passed. He said: If he left her with the intention of not revoking the divorce, she is completely divorced from him and not permissible to him until she marries another husband. And if his intention was to revoke the divorce, then he left her for six months, there is no harm in him revoking the divorce. These two reports are accepted by consensus, because there is no disagreement among the Ummah that when she exits the waiting period, the husband has no claim over her, and she becomes master of her own self.

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: She is completely divorced from him
key_terms.يُرَاجِعَهَا: He revokes the divorce (takes her back)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband divorces his wife twice and then leaves her until her waiting period ends?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the distinction between a revocable divorce (raj'i) and an irrevocable separation (banan) when a husband leaves his wife after two divorces during the waiting period, depending on his intent to revoke or not. It highlights the Shia scholarly consensus that once the iddah concludes, the wife gains autonomy over her person, a principle rooted in the Quranic verses on divorce. The text emphasizes that the husband's intention determines whether the divorce is final or if he retains the right to take her back within the iddah period.
